summary: Modern data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need to move data to external ML systems. Capabilities range from in-database model training (SQL-based ML) and LLM inference via serverless functions to native vector storage and similarity search for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Market momentum is strong, with Gartner projecting 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval for GenAI by 2026 and the vector database market forecast to reach ~USD 17.91 billion by 2034.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Cortex AI — managed LLM and ML functions plus vector search
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex provides serverless SQL and Python functions for LLM tasks (summarize, translate, sentiment, complete, classify), fully managed embedding generation, Cortex Search for semantic retrieval, and Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL. It also extends to Snowflake Postgres, letting developers call Cortex AI functions directly from Postgres workloads.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type and VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / vector distance functions, plus the managed Cortex Search service for semantic retrieval. No third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in access to hosted foundation models (e.g., Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) via COMPLETE and related Cortex functions; no external API keys or infrastructure to manage.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex functions billed by tokens processed (credits per million tokens) plus underlying warehouse/compute and storage. No separate platform fee for Cortex.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML for in-database model training and Vertex AI / Gemini integration for generative AI
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, boosted trees, DNN) using standard SQL. Through remote models it connects to Vertex AI and Gemini for text generation, embeddings, and multimodal inference directly from SQL (ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING).
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports vector storage, VECTOR_SEARCH, and vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) within the warehouse, enabling similarity search without an external vector DB.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models via remote models; also supports importing custom TensorFlow/ONNX models and Hugging Face models through Vertex endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML priced on bytes processed or flat-rate/capacity slots for training and inference; generative/remote model calls incur separate Vertex AI per-call charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for embeddings/vector search and pgai for in-database LLM and embedding workflows
databases.description: pgvector adds a vector column type with similarity operators and ANN indexing (HNSW, IVFFlat) to open-source Postgres. The pgai extension (from Timescale) brings embedding creation, automated vectorization, and LLM calls to providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, Cohere) directly via SQL, keeping AI logic close to the data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Via extension. Core PostgreSQL does not include vector search; it is provided by the pgvector extension. On managed Postgres offerings this is 'built-in' only where the provider ships pgvector by default. Treated here as extension-based native-to-Postgres-ecosystem.
databases.llm_integration: Through pgai, Postgres can call external LLM/embedding APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama) and automatically maintain embeddings; LangChain and other frameworks integrate with pgvector as a vector store.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; costs are only the underlying compute/storage of the Postgres host (self-managed or managed service) plus any external LLM API usage fees.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-based integration with SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock/Comprehend
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models from SQL by integrating Aurora (MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible) with Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon Comprehend. You call hosted models via SQL functions for predictions, sentiment analysis, and generative inference without moving data out of the database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Aurora ML itself does not provide vector search. Aurora PostgreSQL supports vector search only through the pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML feature.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models through SQL function calls; Comprehend for NLP tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra Aurora ML charge; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage/IO costs plus per-request charges from SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend for the invoked models.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — in-warehouse model creation and inference via SQL with SageMaker/Bedrock
databases.description: Redshift ML enables creating, training, and deploying ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, with SageMaker Autopilot handling training behind the scenes. It supports in-database prediction functions and can invoke remote SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Bedrock LLMs for generative tasks directly from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native at the Redshift ML level. Amazon Redshift added vector capabilities separately (e.g., the VECTOR type and similarity functions for some use cases), but Redshift ML as a feature does not provide vector search; dedicated vector workloads typically rely on other AWS services like OpenSearch or Aurora pgvector.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon SageMaker (Autopilot, custom endpoints) and Amazon Bedrock LLMs invoked via SQL functions for generative and inference tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed through standard Redshift compute plus SageMaker training/hosting costs; model training uses SageMaker resources, and inference against remote endpoints incurs those services' per-request fees.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI for model training/serving and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides tooling for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including foundation model APIs, agent frameworks, and MLflow-based lifecycle management. Databricks Vector Search is a managed, serverless vector database integrated with Unity Catalog that auto-syncs embeddings from Delta tables.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a first-party managed vector index with automatic embedding generation and sync from source tables; no external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to hosted and custom LLMs (including Llama, DBRX, and external providers via AI Gateway), with retrieval and agent orchestration tooling.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute and model serving; Vector Search billed on serverless compute and storage. Foundation model APIs priced per token or via provisioned throughput.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search — native vector similarity search on operational document data
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run approximate nearest-neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage with HNSW indexing. It unifies vector, metadata, and full-text search in one query for RAG and semantic search applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is a built-in Atlas capability using dedicated vector indexes and the $vectorSearch operator; no third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with LLM and embedding providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, Cohere, Amazon Bedrock) and frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex for RAG pipelines; embeddings are generated externally and stored in Atlas.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas; vector search runs on Atlas Search Nodes or shared cluster resources, so cost scales with cluster tier/dedicated search node sizing and storage rather than a separate per-query fee.
